title: Getting Data You Can Trust
audience: Clinical researchers and clinician-scientists new to AI
objectives: Audit a consent protocol for comprehension rather than signature.
Cost out the strategies needed to close a representation gap.
Judge whether a security protocol protects against re-identification.
Quantify inter-rater agreement and decide how many labellers are needed.
Map source records to the OMOP common data model using concept IDs.

sections.name: Tab 1 - Consent (Autonomy)
sections.purpose: Judge whether a consent form was actually understood.
sections.how_to_use: Move the language-complexity select_slider from jargon to 'Simplified & empowering' and compare the revised text against the legal standard on the left.

sections.name: Tab 2 - Representation (Justice)
sections.purpose: Cost out what closing a representation gap actually takes.
sections.how_to_use: Name the missing group, set the target-proportion slider, then tick the three strategy checkboxes (community liaisons +10%, translated materials +5%, logistical support +10%). The bar chart and pass/fail verdict update. The baseline is a fixed 5% for passive recruitment.

sections.name: Tab 3 - Security (Privacy)
sections.purpose: Recognise that de-identification alone is not protection.
sections.how_to_use: Tick the four security layers. All four gives SECURE; two or three gives VULNERABLE; fewer gives CRITICAL RISK. The page opens at CRITICAL RISK by design, because nothing is checked yet.

sections.name: Tab 4 - Label Quality
sections.purpose: Establish that a model cannot be more reliable than its labels.
sections.how_to_use: Simulated radiologists label chest X-rays. Set the number of X-rays, radiologists, and the disagreement rate, then read the ICC metric, the high-disagreement table (candidates for re-review), and the accuracy-vs-number-of-annotators curve, whose elbow answers 'how many readers can we afford'.

sections.name: Tab 5 - Common Vocabulary
sections.purpose: Make the data readable outside your own institution.
sections.how_to_use: Set the patient count and seed, then follow the three steps: raw EHR source records, the OMOP person table (names and addresses removed, demographics replaced by concept IDs such as 8507 for male), and condition_occurrence mapped from ICD-10.

chatbot_guidance: The audit target is the IC3 UF public COVID-19 dataset; the subject is a patient and the sample is an electronic health record.

At the default 20% disagreement rate the ICC is negative. That is not a bug: it means the radiologists disagree with each other more than the X-rays differ, so the label carries no signal. The page explains this.
The security tab opens at CRITICAL RISK because nothing is checked yet, not because something is broken.
The OMOP demo runs on both tracks. If asked why concept IDs matter, the answer is that the same query then works at a site that codes in SNOMED.
